skill.name: lead-follow-up
skill.description: Review Reach website leads and booking requests through the Reach MCP server. Draft follow-up messages for owners to send manually, without sending messages or changing lead statuses.
skill.summary: Prioritize new Reach leads and draft short, factual follow-up messages for manual sending.

content.user_title: Review Leads and Draft Follow-Up Messages
content.value_statement: New enquiries and booking requests can remain unanswered when owners lack a clear follow-up list. This skill prioritizes Reach leads and drafts factual messages for owners to send manually.
actual_capabilities: Select an account location and stop when its Google connection is inactive.
Retrieve merged customer leads or raw booking requests from the Reach website.
Filter records by status and date range, with retrieval limits up to 200.
Prioritize new or unviewed requests and display at most 10 records at a time.
Draft short WhatsApp or SMS messages and email versions when a customer email is present.
Use recorded names, services, and preferred slots without inventing prices, availability, or missing details.
limitations: Requires the hosted Reach MCP server, browser OAuth sign-in, and an active Google connection.
Reads leads from Reach website booking forms, not every Google Business Profile contact channel.
Does not send customer messages or change lead statuses; feature requests require separate owner confirmation.
Phone numbers remain masked, and retrieval limits or returned restrictions can prevent a complete lead list.

use_cases.title: Review Unanswered Enquiries
use_cases.description: A local business owner reviews new website leads and selects customers who need a short follow-up draft.

use_cases.title: Prepare Booking Replies
use_cases.description: A receptionist reviews booking requests and drafts replies using recorded services and preferred times without claiming confirmed availability.

use_cases.title: Review a Location's Request History
use_cases.description: An agency account manager selects a client location, examines its raw booking log, and reports date coverage and retrieval limits.

prompt_templates.title: List New Leads
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my new Reach leads, with the newest first. Ask which location if needed, and show no more than 10.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review enquiries before drafting replies.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Short Reply
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a short SMS for the lead I select. Use only recorded details, ask for a suitable time, and do not send it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: prepare one message for manual sending.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recent Bookings
prompt_templates.prompt: Show raw booking requests for [location] between [start ISO date-time] and [end ISO date-time]. Prioritize unviewed requests and state any coverage limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review a specific location and period.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Multichannel Follow-Ups
prompt_templates.prompt: For [location] and [date range], review new leads and show 10 at a time. Draft SMS and available email versions for leads I select. Use [language], avoid unsupported claims, and disclose retrieval limits. Do not send messages or change statuses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare several drafts with explicit scope and language.

output_examples.input: Draft an SMS for a selected lead named Maya. No service or preferred time is recorded.
output_examples.output: Hi Maya, thank you for your enquiry. What day and time would suit you for an appointment?

output_examples.input: A selected lead named Noah requested a consultation on Tuesday afternoon and has an email address. Draft an email without assuming availability.
output: Hi Noah, thank you for your consultation enquiry.
Would another time also suit you if that slot is unavailable?

output_examples.input: Explain how to contact a selected lead whose phone number is masked.
output_examples.output: The phone number is masked. Open the lead in the Reach dashboard to view the full number and send your message manually.

best_practices: Confirm the location and date range before reviewing customer records.
Check returned limitations and missing fields before drawing conclusions or drafting messages.
Review each draft, keep customer details separate, and send messages manually through the appropriate channel.
anti_patterns: Treating the retrieved list as complete when limits or returned restrictions apply.
Inventing missing services, prices, availability, addresses, or full phone numbers.
Requesting automatic message sending or including one customer's private details in another customer's reply.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Connect the Reach MCP server in your AI client and sign in through browser OAuth. The Google connection must be active.

faq.question: Where do the leads come from?
faq.answer: Leads come from booking forms on the owner's Reach website. The skill does not claim to cover every Google contact channel.

faq.question: Does the skill send messages or update statuses?
faq.answer: No. Owners send drafted messages manually, and the skill does not change lead statuses.

faq.question: How are leads different from bookings?
faq.answer: The leads view merges repeat requests from the same person. The bookings view shows the raw request log with notes and viewed status.

faq.question: Can I retrieve a complete phone number?
faq.answer: No. Phone numbers are masked to the last four digits. Open the lead in the Reach dashboard to view the full number.

faq.question: Can I filter records and draft in another language?
faq.answer: Yes. Filter by status and ISO date-time range. Drafts use the lead's language or the language you request.
